heroHeadline: Day 587: US Formally Recognizes Mexico's Security Strategy; Armed Attack on Former Governor Rocha Moya's Culiacán Residence; México Canta Binational Music Contest Launched
heroSubtitle: On May 11, 2026 (Day 587), President Sheinbaum returned to the National Palace for her Monday mañanera after concluding her three-day Sonora working tour. Five major developments: (1) The U.S. government announced it would formally publish a document recognizing Mexico's security strategy centered on 'Attention to Causes' — including anti-weapons-trafficking efforts — a notable diplomatic shift after months of escalating tensions. (2) An armed attack struck the former personal residence of Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya (on 30-day leave) in Culiacán's Las Quintas neighborhood — multiple gunshots at approximately 10:12 AM, no injuries. Sheinbaum disclosed the incident at the mañanera. (3) Sheinbaum launched 'México Canta 2026,' a binational music contest for young Mexicans and Mexican-Americans promoting regional music that doesn't normalize violence (featuring Majo Aguilar and Junior H). (4) She defended Education Secretary Mario Delgado over the 2025–2026 school calendar — unanimously approved by all 31 state education secretaries plus CDMX — criticizing governors who later reversed their position. (5) Cuba-bound humanitarian aid departed that day, reaffirming Mexico's rejection of the U.S. blockade. Ongoing backdrop: Trump's review of all 53 Mexican consulates continues; Banxico has cut its rate to 6.50% (terminal rate, no further cuts expected through 2027); USMCA first formal negotiating round remains on track for the week of May 25.
